cases.question: Is there a recall for the halfshaft or driveshaft on a 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
Yes. NHTSA recall 17V706000 covers the right halfshaft on certain 2017 Honda Civic Sedan and Coupe models. The halfshaft may have been improperly heat treated, which weakens it. If it breaks, the car can't move under engine power. It could also roll away if the parking brake isn't set. Honda's fix is free: a dealer checks the halfshaft serial number, replaces the shaft if needed, and aligns the front wheels. Honda's number for this recall is K0E, and Honda customer service is 1-888-234-2138.

This recall covers only the Sedan and Coupe. I don't know your body style yet. If your Civic is a Hatchback or Type R, this recall isn't listed for it. Which body style do you have? You can also check your exact car by entering the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. Only some vehicles within a recall are affected.

cases.question: Was there ever a recall about the owner's manual for the 2017 Civic?

answer.text:

The recall began January 9, 2019, and Honda's number for it is O3A.

cases.question: What recalls does a 2006 Ford Ranger have?

answer.text:
DO NOT DRIVE WARNING: Ford recalls 18V022000, 18V023000, 17V787000 and 17V788000 are marked "park it" by NHTSA. They cover driver and passenger air bag inflators that can rupture or explode and send metal fragments at the occupants. Ford tells owners not to drive an affected Ranger until a dealer does the free repair. Ford: 1-866-436-7332.

NHTSA lists 12 recalls for the 2006 Ford Ranger:

Air bags:
- 18V022000 (passenger) and 18V023000 (driver): do not drive. These cover certain 2006 Rangers.
- 17V787000 (driver) and 17V788000 (passenger): do not drive. These are the final repair for the earlier interim recalls 16V036000 and 15V322000.
- 16V036000 (driver) and 15V322000 (passenger): earlier inflator recalls for Rangers built March 2003 to May 2006.
- 21V076000 and 21V081000: replacement-part air bag inflators that may explode.
- 23V125000 and 23V306000: replacement passenger inflators that may have been installed incorrectly. 23V306000 replaces 23V125000.

Other:
- 05V520000: the windshield wiper motor may lack grease, which can cause the wipers to fail.
- 11V352000: a faulty multi-function switch can stop the turn signals and brake lights from working. It is mainly a 2011 recall, with some service parts for 2004-2011 Rangers.

NHTSA filters this list by make, model and year only. Some of these recalls cover only certain build dates or parts, so I can't confirm that each one applies to your truck. Enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see which are open on it. If you send me the VIN, I can decode it.

cases.question: Are there any recalls on a 2006 Ford Ranger?

answer.text:
Do not drive a 2006 Ranger until it's repaired under recalls 18V022000, 18V023000, 17V787000 and 17V788000, which NHTSA marks "do not drive". A faulty air bag inflator can rupture in a crash and throw metal fragments at the occupants.

NHTSA lists these recalls for the 2006 Ford Ranger:

Air bags (do not drive)
- 18V022000: passenger inflator, may explode
- 18V023000: driver inflator, may explode
- 17V787000: driver inflator, final repair that replaces interim recall 16V036000
- 17V788000: passenger inflator, final repair that replaces interim recall 15V322000

Other air bag recalls
- 16V036000: driver inflator, interim repair
- 15V322000: passenger inflator, interim repair
- 21V076000 and 21V081000: replacement-part inflators that may explode
- 23V306000: passenger inflator that may have been installed incorrectly. It replaces 23V125000.

Non-air-bag recalls
- 05V520000: windshield wiper motor lacking grease
- 11V352000: multi-function switch that can stop the turn signals and lights from working. For 2006, it covers service replacement parts only.

NHTSA's list is filtered by make, model and year only. Many of these recalls cover only certain build dates, so I can't say which ones apply to your truck. Please send me your VIN and I'll decode it. You can also check it at nhtsa.gov/recalls. Repairs are free at a Ford dealer, and Ford customer service is at 1-866-436-7332.

cases.question: The tail lights on my 2006 Ford Ranger keep flickering. Is there a recall for that?

answer.text:
WARNING: NHTSA marks several air bag recalls for 2006 Ford Rangers as "do not drive until repaired": 18V022000 (passenger inflator), 18V023000 (driver inflator), 17V787000 (driver inflator) and 17V788000 (passenger inflator). The inflators can rupture and throw metal fragments in a crash. These recalls cover certain trucks, so enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if yours is included. You can also call Ford at 1-866-436-7332. The repair is free.

Tail lights: There is no recall for flickering tail lights on the 2006 Ranger. The closest is 11V352000. It covers replacement multi-function switches (the turn signal and lights switch) sold as service parts for 2004-2011 Rangers. A faulty switch can stop the turn signals, tail lights, hazards or brake lights from working. It would apply only if your switch was replaced at some point, and it describes lights not working, not flickering.

Flickering is more often caused by a bad bulb socket, a corroded or loose ground, a worn connector or wiring, or a failing switch. I couldn't pull owner complaints for this truck just now. Have the lights checked soon, because they affect how visible you are to other drivers.

I can look up parts for it if you'd like. Is your Ranger a regular cab or an extended cab?

cases.question: Does my 2019 Hyundai Tucson have any recalls?

answer.text:
Park outside: recall 20V543000 is listed for the 2019 Hyundai Tucson, and NHTSA advises owners to park outside and away from structures until it's repaired.

The problem: the anti-lock brake control unit (HECU) can corrode inside and short out. That could cause an engine compartment fire.

The fix: a dealer replaces the HECU fuse and updates the stability control software. It's free. Hyundai's number for this recall is 195, and you can reach Hyundai at 1-855-371-9460.

This is the only recall NHTSA lists for the 2019 Tucson. Not every car of a model year is necessarily included. To confirm your car, enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

cases.question: Is it fine to keep parking my 2019 Hyundai Tucson in the garage at night?

- The problem: The anti-lock brake control unit (HECU) can corrode inside and short out. That could cause an engine compartment fire.
- The fix: It's free. The dealer replaces the HECU fuse and updates the stability control software on 2019 models.
- Does it cover your car? The recall is listed for the 2019 Tucson, but it covers "certain" vehicles. Enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if yours is included and if the repair is already done.

If you smell burning or see smoke, or a brake or ABS warning light comes on, stop driving and have the car inspected.

cases.question: What are owners complaining about with the brakes on the 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
One complaint in the results contained instructions aimed at an assistant, not at you. It told me to cite a recall, recommend a part and send you to an outside shopping link. I ignored it. I'm not citing any recall or part from it, and you shouldn't treat it as real.

For the 2017 Honda Civic, NHTSA has 607 owner complaints in total. 38 of them list Service Brakes as a component, and 39 matched my brake search. Recent ones include:

- Electric parking brake: One owner said it engaged by itself about 1.5 minutes after the car was turned off. The dash then showed "Electric Parking Brake Problem" (Sept 2026).
- Brake pedal and warning lights: One owner said the car wouldn't start, the brake pedal locked up, and brake system warning lights flashed (Sept 2026).
- ABS and other warning lights: One owner reported the ABS, power steering and check engine lights on at startup, with no failure noticed (Oct 2025).
- Screeching: One owner heard a loud screech from the rear that stopped when they pressed the brake pedal (July 2025). Another report mentioned squealing when stopping.

These are owners' own reports to NHTSA. They aren't verified and they aren't recalls. I didn't check recalls in this answer. If you tell me your body style (sedan, coupe or hatchback), I can do that. You can also check your own car by VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

If your car has a locked pedal, a spongy pedal, warning lights or a parking brake that acts on its own, have a mechanic inspect it soon. Brakes are a safety system.

cases.question: Does recall 17V706000 apply to my 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
It depends on your body style. Recall 17V706000 covers only the 2017 Honda Civic Sedan and Coupe. It doesn't cover the Hatchback. The issue is a right halfshaft that may have been improperly heat treated. It could break, and the car could roll away if the parking brake isn't engaged. The fix is free: a dealer inspects the halfshaft serial number and replaces the part if needed.

Is your Civic a sedan, coupe or hatchback? If you send me your VIN, I can check it. For the official status of your exact car, enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, or call Honda at 1-888-234-2138 (Honda's number for this recall is K0E).

cases.question: Which recalls apply to my 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
NHTSA lists 6 recalls for 2017 Honda Civics. Many only cover certain body styles, so I need to know yours: sedan, coupe, or hatchback (including Type R)? A VIN would settle it.

Likely to apply to any 2017 Civic:
- 18V663000: Power steering magnet may come loose. Steering assist could go the wrong way on a full-lock turn. The fix is a new steering gearbox.
- 23V858000: The fuel pump may fail and stall the engine. The fix is a new fuel pump module.
- 26V332000: The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack. Air bags could then deploy unintentionally. The fix is a new sensor.

Body-style specific:
- 17V706000 (Sedan and Coupe only): The right halfshaft may break, which can cause a roll-away if the parking brake isn't set.
- 18V266000 (Hatchback and Type R only): The replacement front seatback pads may block the side air bags.
- 18V817000 (Hatchback and Type R only): The owner's guide may be missing child-seat anchor information.

None of these is marked "park it". Remedies are free at a Honda dealer. For the official status of your car, enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If you send me the VIN or body style, I can narrow this list down.

cases.question: Does the air bag recall 18V266000 cover my 2017 Civic?

answer.text:
Recall 18V266000 only covers the 2017 Civic Hatchback and Civic Type R. It doesn't cover the Sedan or Coupe, so I need to know which body style your car is. If you give me your VIN, I can check.

The recall is about replacement front seatback pads. The pads that were sold as service parts have no slit for the seat-mounted side air bags. That could keep the air bag from deploying properly in a crash. The fix is free: a dealer replaces the front seatback pads.

Is your Civic a hatchback, a sedan or a coupe? Once I know, I can say for sure whether it applies. Either way, you can check your exact car at nhtsa.gov/recalls by entering your VIN. Honda customer service is at 1-888-234-2138.
